question: What is the simple definition of a wound?

options.A: A permanent scar left after surgery
options.B: A swelling caused by fluid accumulation under the skin
options.C: An infection deep inside the muscle tissue
options.D: A break in the integrity of the skin or mucous membranes

explanation: A wound is any disruption to the normal structure and function of the skin or mucous membranes. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is classifying wounds properly important in midwifery practice?

options.A: It entirely prevents scars from forming after a tear
options.B: It replaces the need for using sterile surgical instruments
options.C: It eliminates the need to document daily wound checks
options.D: It helps choose the right care plan and spot early infections

explanation: Classifying wounds guides clinical management, helps predict healing, and allows midwives to catch complications early. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which wound type is a clean, straight cut made by a sharp instrument?
explanation: An incision is created by a sharp blade, resulting in neat, straight edges with minimal surrounding tissue damage. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h2)

question: A mother sustains a jagged, irregular tear in the perineum due to rapid baby delivery. What type of wound is this?
explanation: Tears caused by stretching or blunt force trauma result in jagged, irregular wound edges known as lacerations. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which skin layer is affected in a superficial wound?
explanation: Superficial wounds are restricted to the outermost layer of the skin, the epidermis. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a main feature of full-thickness wounds compared to superficial ones?

options.A: They only affect the top layer of skin and heal in a few hours
options.B: They heal entirely through simple surface cell regeneration
options.C: They extend into subcutaneous fat, muscle, or bone and require scarring to heal
options.D: They never require any form of cleaning or dressing

explanation: Full-thickness wounds involve deep tissue loss below the dermis, necessitating granulation and scar tissue formation for repair. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following describes a clean wound?

options.A: An uninfected surgical wound where sterile tracts are not entered
options.B: A surgical incision that is currently draining thick pus
options.C: An open accidental wound exposed to dirt and soil
options.D: A deep tear contaminated with bowel contents

explanation: Clean wounds are operative wounds with no inflammation and no entry into colonized tracts like the gastrointestinal or genital systems. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h4)

question: A postnatal mother has a perineal tear that shows pus, redness, and a bad odor. How is this wound classified?
explanation: The presence of pus, foul odor, and localized inflammation indicates that active microbial infection has developed. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is an episiotomy?

options.A: An infection of the uterine lining after delivery
options.B: A surgical incision of the perineum made during childbirth
options.C: A superficial skin scrape on the maternal abdomen
options.D: A natural tear involving the rectal mucosa

explanation: An episiotomy is a deliberate surgical cut made in the perineal tissues to facilitate the delivery of the baby. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which degree of perineal tear extends deep enough to involve the rectal lining?
explanation: Fourth-degree perineal tears are severe injuries that extend completely through the anal sphincter and into the rectal mucosa. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a key reason for conducting regular wound checks?

options.A: To ensure the patient never feels any pain during healing
options.B: To catch early signs of complications and guide care decisions
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for wound dressings
options.D: To speed up natural skin color restoration after trauma

explanation: Regular assessment allows midwives to monitor healing progress and detect early complications like infection or wound breakdown. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT checked during a routine wound assessment?

options.A: The depth and size of the wound
options.B: The amount and type of wound drainage
options.D: The condition of the surrounding skin

explanation: Shoe size has no relevance to wound assessment, whereas drainage, surrounding skin health, and wound dimensions are vital clinical indicators. [learn more](BMP120_U3_T1#BMP120_U3_T1_h6)
